description: The non-framebuffer gates. Two kinds live here. 'savestate' runs --diag-savestate-roundtrip and IS gated: it compares a continuously-played NES against an identical one that did a SaveState+LoadState round trip mid-play, frame by frame, and fails if any state the savestate is responsible for came back different. (A framebuffer-only immediate difference is expected and benign - the framebuffer is a render target, not machine state - and that is why the verdict string below says so; the false failure that used to come from treating it as a fault was fixed on 2026-09-02.) 'benchmark' runs --benchmark and is INFORMATIONAL ONLY: timing is machine-dependent, so it is printed and never affects the exit code.

cases.description: Savestate round trip on a bundled story ROM with the accuracy-target cores.
Same round trip on the FMC family, so a serialisation regression in one family cannot hide behind the other.
A second story ROM, so the savestate gate is not a property of one ROM.
Savestate round trip on MMC3/SMB3 - mapper bank state and scanline-IRQ counters are the parts of a savestate most likely to be forgotten. SKIPs when the 65-o-borked corpus is not on the machine.

Mega Man 3 (the db's 'savestates don''t work' title). LoadState never read back the fractional-cycle accumulator, so a savestate only round-tripped at frames where it was already 0 (every 60th in default mode - warmups 180/300/900 all hid it). This point is deliberately off that grid, and loads into a fresh machine.

The same on the default FMC cores - the defect was board-level, so it hit every core players use. LoadState never read back the fractional-cycle accumulator, so a savestate only round-tripped at frames where it was already 0 (every 60th in default mode - warmups 180/300/900 all hid it). This point is deliberately off that grid, and loads into a fresh machine.

NTSC timing keeps its own dot budget and parity toggle, now part of the savestate. LoadState never read back the fractional-cycle accumulator, so a savestate only round-tripped at frames where it was already 0 (every 60th in default mode - warmups 180/300/900 all hid it). This point is deliberately off that grid, and loads into a fresh machine.

New game (register a name, start file 1), open the pause menu in the North Palace at 830, close it at 960, walk right. The frame after the menu closes polls sprite 0 twice; a $2002 read used to clear the sprite-0 flag with VBlank, so the second poll spun forever - HUD blanked, sprites gone, game hung. Matches Mesen 2.1.1 on every sample of this route in both timing modes. The pre-fix build hashes C62AD0E3979D8D9B (9 colours).

Precise mode: frame clock plus PPU_FIX's mid-line latches (dot-257 horizontal latch, render address, pending sprite-0 dot, odd-frame parity). LoadState never read back the fractional-cycle accumulator, so a savestate only round-tripped at frames where it was already 0 (every 60th in default mode - warmups 180/300/900 all hid it). This point is deliberately off that grid, and loads into a fresh machine.

INFORMATIONAL. Speed of the accuracy-target stack. Never gates. Its point is the FIX-vs-FMC delta on the line below: the project policy is that an accuracy fix which meaningfully regresses speed for marginal gain should be rejected, and this row is how you notice.
